footer_fields.label: Reference metadata
footer_fields.value: Eurostat Metadata – SDG 13.10: Domestic net greenhouse gas emissions

national_indicator_definition: For Bosnia and Herzegovina, the indicator is based on data from the National Inventory Document (NID) of Bosnia and Herzegovina, prepared and submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). National data cover greenhouse gas emissions expressed in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent, in accordance with the methodology of the national greenhouse gas inventory. For presentation on this portal, the series of total emissions excluding sinks from land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) is used.
national_rationale: The indicator enables monitoring of changes in total greenhouse gas emissions in Bosnia and Herzegovina over time and provides a national presentation of the EU SDG indicator 13.10. The data are based on the official national greenhouse gas inventory submitted by Bosnia and Herzegovina to the UNFCCC. The latest source used is the 2024 National Inventory Document (NID) of Bosnia and Herzegovina, submitted to the UNFCCC on 13 August 2026.
national_methodology_characteristics: The national data are taken from the National Inventory Document of Bosnia and Herzegovina (NID) and expressed in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. For monitoring progress on the portal, an emissions index with 1990 as the base year was calculated, with the value for 1990 set to 100. The index is calculated as the value of emissions in the observed year divided by the value of emissions in 1990, multiplied by 100. For the assessment of progress, the I90 (1990=100) series is used. Since a reduction in emissions represents the desired direction for this indicator, progress is configured with a negative direction (direction: negative). On the portal, 2015 is set as the base year for the progress calculation, while 2030 is specified as the target year in the indicator configuration. A decrease in the index value therefore represents a favourable direction of change. This progress calculation represents the configuration used for the national presentation of the indicator on the BHAS portal and does not constitute a separate Eurostat progress methodology specifically established for Bosnia and Herzegovina.
national_long_objective: Reduce greenhouse gas emissions compared with the 1990 level, in accordance with the commitments and objectives of Bosnia and Herzegovina under the UNFCCC and its national climate policies.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator measures total national emissions from both the sectors covered by the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) and sectors outside the ETS (ESD), covering the so-called Kyoto basket of greenhouse gases. This includes carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O) and F-gases, namely hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), nitrogen trifluoride (NF₃) and sulphur hexafluoride (SF₆), from all sectors of the greenhouse gas inventories. Estimated emissions from international aviation and maritime transport are excluded for individual countries. The indicator is presented both as net emissions including land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) and excluding LULUCF. Using the individual global warming potentials (GWPs) of each gas, emissions are integrated into a single indicator expressed in CO₂ equivalents. The data are based on annual greenhouse gas inventory reporting under the UNFCCC and are provided to Eurostat by the European Environment Agency (EEA).
eu_rationale: The indicator is used to monitor progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 13 on climate action. The European Climate Law sets a target of reducing net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 compared with 1990 and achieving climate neutrality by 2050. The “Fit for 55” package comprises interconnected measures in the areas of energy, transport, taxation and climate policy.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator is updated annually. Eurostat states that data for individual countries are based on greenhouse gas inventory reporting under the UNFCCC, provided to Eurostat by the EEA. The time series starts in 1990 and the indicator is available in three forms: million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent, tonnes of CO₂ equivalent per capita and an index with 1990=100.
eu_long_objective: Reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% compared with the 1990 level by 2030 and achieve climate neutrality by 2050.
